subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this ten-table residual durable shared-state boundary before any recovery/runtime consumer is merged?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent, but choosing a new cross-owner persistence model and shared-state lifecycle contract is a core architecture decision that cannot be resolved from tests alone.

options.title: Accept the residual boundary
options.body: Sponsor the narrow shared-state model and review this PR as the owned persistence foundation for later consumer slices.

options.title: Narrow before implementation
options.body: Identify facts that must remain in existing task, flow, subagent, session, or delivery owners, then ask for a reduced storage proposal.

options.title: Reject a generic durable layer
options.body: Keep cross-owner recovery work within existing owner-specific APIs and close the proposed foundation as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Narrow before implementation
recommendation.body: Identify facts that must remain in existing task, flow, subagent, session, or delivery owners, then ask for a reduced storage proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available contact for the proposal’s intended boundaries; no upstream core decision owner is identifiable from the supplied review context.
